recent_posts.title: My Experience Switching to a Split Keyboard (Corne V4)
recent_posts.summary: A software engineer shares their experience switching to the Corne V4 split keyboard after suffering from wrist and hand pain. The post covers the adjustment period (dropping to 15-30 WPM initially), the column-staggered layout benefits, custom key layout configuration using layers for numbers and symbols, Neovim-specific optimizations like moving Escape near home row, and the long-term outcome: eliminated wrist pain and improved typing speed by ~30 WPM. Includes honest advice on who should and shouldn't consider a split keyboard (not recommended for heavy Blender users).

recent_posts.title: My Favorite Neovim Colorschemes
recent_posts.summary: A curated walkthrough of favorite Neovim colorschemes including a custom personal scheme based on cosec twilight, base16 black metal Gorgoth, vague.nvim, Zenburn, Gruber Darker, and Zen Written. Each scheme is discussed in terms of contrast, eye strain, and ideal usage contexts (late night coding vs. bright office environments). Tips are also shared for discovering lesser-known colorschemes by following text editor enthusiast communities and exploring schemes from other editors like Helix.

recent_posts.title: Why developers need hobbies outside of coding
recent_posts.summary: Coding can become all-consuming, crowding out other hobbies and interests. While passion is valuable, over-specialization early in your career limits creativity and project ideas. Maintaining diverse hobbies outside programming provides fresh perspectives, inspires meaningful projects, and expands your comfort zone. Balance enhances rather than diminishes your coding abilities, giving you real-world problems to solve instead of optimizing tools endlessly. Stepping into uncomfortable new areas translates to better adaptability as a developer.

recent_posts.title: How to Switch to Neovim (Tips & Roadmap)
recent_posts.summary: A practical roadmap for transitioning to Neovim, starting with learning Vim motions in your current editor (like VS Code), then becoming comfortable with terminal usage, and finally building a custom Neovim configuration from scratch. The guide emphasizes gradual learning of essential keybindings rather than memorizing everything at once, recommends resources like kickstart.nvim and TJ DeVries' tutorial series, and advises against using pre-configured distributions initially to better understand core Neovim concepts.

recent_posts.title: Making a 3D Model Viewer in C | Ep. 3
Making a 3D Model Viewer in C | Ep. 2
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step tutorial on creating the first triangle in a 3D model viewer using C and OpenGL. Covers the graphics pipeline fundamentals, vertex buffer creation, shader development with GLSL, and cross-platform shader compilation using sokol-shdc. Demonstrates how to upload vertex data to the GPU, create vertex and fragment shaders, set up the rendering pipeline, and add color interpolation to create a colorful triangle.

recent_posts.title: Making a 3D Model Viewer in C | Ep. 1
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to building a 3D model viewer from scratch using C and the Sokol graphics library. Covers project setup, window creation, and basic graphics initialization with cross-platform windowing abstractions. The tutorial demonstrates how to set up a minimal graphics application that opens a window with a colored background, preparing the foundation for more advanced 3D rendering features.

recent_posts.title: Making Web games in Go is Easy (Ebitengine)
recent_posts.summary: Demonstrates how to create web games using Go and Ebitengine by building a simple animated sprite game and deploying it as WebAssembly. Covers the complete workflow from setting up a basic Ebitengine project to compiling it for web deployment, including using development tools like watchexec for rapid prototyping with automatic recompilation and live reloading.

recent_posts.title: How to setup Terminal Cursor Animations (3 Methods)
recent_posts.summary: Three methods for adding cursor animations to terminals: using Kitty terminal's built-in cursor trail feature with simple configuration, installing the smearcursor.nvim plugin for Neovim that works across any terminal, and building Ghostty terminal from source to use custom cursor trail shaders. Each approach has different compatibility requirements and visual effects.
